text:
alex: Quick heads-up — after today's perf run the Mixtral <-> draft pairing + speculative decode shows higher tail latency when tokenizer splits occur. Posting short profile and ideas. @sasha @maria

sasha: Can you paste the profile/output? Is this on Dedicated or Hosted canary?

alex: Hosted canary (region eu-west1). Summary below, full trace uploaded to CI.
```
kernel_select: aten_autotuned
batching: dynamic (max_batch=32, target_latency=120ms)
spec_accept_rate: 0.35
rope_scale: 1.12
kv_head_dim: 128
kv_heads: 32
kv_hit_rate_warm: 0.87
latencies_ms: {p50:45, p95:210, p99:480}
notes: pairing picks Mixtral-draft (tokenizer mismatch with Qwen-family), token splits increase tokens/sec & decoding retries
```

maria: Yikes. Tokenizer mismatch is the common culprit — Mixtral uses byte-BPE variant and our draft Llama uses standard BPE; extra splits cause speculative to accept suboptimal drafts. Are we normalizing whitespace and utf-nfc?

liam: Two levers: (1) normalize tokenizer output pre-pairing (cheap CPU), (2) restrict speculative pairing to family-compatible models. Tradeoff: (1) reduces mismatch but adds ~6-8% CPU per request, (2) reduces pairing opportunities and may raise average latency/cost.

perf-bot: profiling job #981 finished — flamegraph: https://ci.redwood/profiles/981 (private) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sasha: If we tune RoPE from 1.12 -> 1.00 what did you observe on logits / stability? Any impact on caching or kv layout?

alex: Quick microbench locally: lowering rope_scale to 1.00 reduced hallucination in long-context evals and lowered p95 from 210ms -> 180ms on that canary, but kv_hit_rate dropped ~3% (more cache churn because shifted attention weights). So lower rope helps quality+latency tail but costs a bit of reuse.

maria: Hmm. For immediate mitigation I propose: 
- add a tiny tokenizer-normalizer step before speculative pairing (trim repeated spaces, NFC normalize, simple byte canonicalization)
- raise spec_accept_threshold from 0.35 -> 0.55 (fewer bad accepts)
- restrict pairing to models with tokenization_compatibility >= 0.8 (family tag)
- add observability: new console metric `spec-mismatch-rate` + per-route `spec-reject-cost`

liam: SGTM. Note raising accept threshold will increase fallback to base model and therefore increase observed latency for those requests. We should canary with traffic split and track p95/p99 + added CPU.

alex: I'll draft a small rollout PR: canary 10% traffic, 2h window, compare p95/p99, spec-accept-rate, spec-mismatch-rate, kv-hit-rate, cost delta. Will tag eng-runtime and perf.

sasha: Also add a quick kernel selection tweak: prefer `aten_autotuned` for Mixtral lengths > 1024, else prefer `cuda_fused` for short sequences — that reduced memcpy overhead in bench.

liam: Good call. @alex ping when PR is up and I'll coordinate the canary.

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/inference/merge_requests/4021 — includes tokenizer normalizer + accept=0.55 + family filter + metric. Canary started in 5m.

perf-bot: Canary initiated (id=canary-4021) — monitoring dashboards live: https://console.redwood/canaries/4021

maria: Thanks all — follow-up action: collect 2h canary data, then decide on default flags. I'll add a short eval suite for long-context hallucination to the PR checklist. :thumbsup:
